name: AppLlama
tagline: Describe an app in plain language and get a generated, deployable web app without writing the scaffolding yourself.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a product category where the DIY question is unusually funny: the thing you would use to replace it is the same class of tool that powers it. A coding agent can absolutely build you a local generator, a CLI that takes a prompt, calls a model API, writes a project, installs deps, runs the build, and feeds errors back until it compiles. What you cannot cheaply rebuild is everything wrapped around the generation: hosted previews on a URL you can send someone, provisioned databases, auth boilerplate that actually works, and the accumulated prompt scaffolding that keeps output from drifting into nonsense. If you are a developer, the local version is arguably better because you own the files and skip the middle layer. If you wanted this precisely because you did not want to touch a terminal, self-hosting a terminal tool is not a replacement.
coreLoopDIY: A local CLI that turns a plain-language app description into a working scaffolded project, then loops on build errors until it compiles and runs.
requirements: Node 20+ and a terminal you are willing to live in
An LLM API key with real spend on it, since iteration loops burn tokens
Somewhere to deploy if you want a shareable URL, which the local build does not give you
whatYouLose: Hosted preview URLs you can hand to someone who does not have your laptop
Managed database and auth provisioning, which is most of the boring work in any real app
The vendor's tuned system prompts and templates, which are the difference between output that runs and output that almost runs
A browser UI, so non-developers get nothing out of the DIY version
Someone else eating the cost and blame when a generation loop goes sideways
moatNotes: The moat is not the model, which anyone can rent. It is the hosting, provisioning and template layer that turns raw generation into something a non-developer can actually click on.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the value being sold is not code generation, it is the removal of every step around it. Signing up for a model API, managing keys, picking a stack, provisioning a database, wiring auth, and finding a host are each individually easy and collectively the reason most ideas die in a folder. People pay to skip that, and a local CLI that dumps a project into ./my-app does not skip it. Developers who already have the terminal, the keys and the deploy habit are the ones who should not pay.
notes: Using a coding agent to replace an AI app builder is closing a loop that was probably always going to close.
prompt:
Build a local command line app generator called "llamalite". No accounts, no telemetry, no cloud services beyond one LLM API call.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Node 20 with TypeScript, run via tsx
- commander for the CLI
- The Anthropic Messages API called over plain fetch, key read from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env via dotenv
- Generated projects use Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind, nothing else

Behaviour:
1. `llamalite new "a habit tracker with a weekly grid and local storage"` creates ./output/{slug}/.
2. Copy a bundled Vite React Tailwind starter template from ./template into the new folder. Do not ask the model to generate config files, package.json, or tsconfig. Those are fixed.
3. Send the description to the model and require a JSON response: an array of objects with `path` and `contents`, restricted to files under src/. Reject any path that escapes src/ or touches config.
4. Write the files, run `npm install`, then run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build`.
5. If either fails, send the model the error output plus the current contents of the files it wrote and ask for a corrected full file set. Retry up to 3 times, then stop and print the last error.
6. On success print the folder path and the `npm run dev` command.
7. `llamalite iterate {slug} "add a dark mode toggle"` reruns the same loop against the existing src/ files.

Also build:
- A `runs/` log per project: prompt, each model response, each build result, token counts and a rough cost line.
- Sensible retry and timeout handling on the API call.

Explicitly out of scope: hosting, deployment, database provisioning, auth, a web UI, multi user anything, billing, any model other than the one configured. Do not add them.

Deliverables: README with setup in under ten lines, .env.example, the template folder, and one working example run committed as output/example/.
